columns.name: id
columns.semantic_contract: `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`; stable local registry identity and physical parent key.

columns.name: provider_kind
columns.semantic_contract: `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'unknown'`; bounded non-empty parser and normalization adapter identity. Application producers always supply it explicitly; `unknown` is reserved for direct legacy-style compatibility inserts.

columns.name: name
columns.semantic_contract: `TEXT NOT NULL`; user-facing source label.

columns.name: root_path
columns.semantic_contract: `TEXT NOT NULL`; configured local scan root or source locator; runtime values remain outside tracked docs.

columns.name: profile_color
columns.semantic_contract: nullable `TEXT`; green, blue, orange, yellow, red or gray. Session TOML owns the choice; null uses the provider default.

columns.name: profile_position
columns.semantic_contract: `INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 2147483647`, nonnegative; projection of TOML array position. Omitted retained profiles sort last, then by ID.

columns.name: last_scanned_at
columns.semantic_contract: nullable `TEXT`; time recorded for the latest source-level scan attempt, whether it succeeded or not.

columns.name: last_scan_success_at
columns.semantic_contract: nullable `TEXT`; latest source-level attempt that completed or found a readable empty root. Errors do not advance it.

columns.name: last_scan_status
columns.semantic_contract: nullable `TEXT`; latest outcome: `completed`, `empty`, `unavailable`, `configuration_error`, or `scan_failed`. Null means the source has not yet been synchronized under this contract.

columns.name: last_scan_error
columns.semantic_contract: nullable `TEXT`; application-bounded failure consequence for the latest unsuccessful attempt, never a raw exception or source content. Successful attempts clear it.

columns.name: created_at
columns.semantic_contract: `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`; registry creation time.

constraints.documented: `id` is the sole primary key; fresh DDL bounds `last_scan_status`

semantics.class_contract: Normalized from still-available local sources; rescans can recreate content, though stable relational IDs must be preserved during ordinary refreshes.
semantics.deletion_effect: physical parent of `source_files`, `sessions`, `usage_records`, and `context_documents`, all `ON DELETE CASCADE`, and retained `skill_observations` with `NO ACTION`. The latter prevents deleting a source with historical skill evidence. Deleting another source would remove normalized descendants and can invalidate application-enforced links or search rows, so no cleanup is implied.
semantics.documented_constraints: `id` is the sole primary key; fresh DDL bounds `last_scan_status`
semantics.lifecycle_contract: source-derived registry. It is reproducible from configuration and registered roots, but its IDs are physical parents, so ordinary scans update rows in place.
semantics.producers: `ingest/sync/storage.py` through the `ingest/scanner.py` coordinator; `persistence/migrations/` reads provider kinds when migration changes must stale Session inputs.
semantics.purpose_and_authority: one registry row per local source. Session profiles use the existing numeric `id` in version-2 `session-sources.toml`, public settings APIs and new filter links. `provider_kind` selects parsing and normalization; `name`, `profile_color` and `profile_position` project the configured label, palette color and TOML array order. Local Context remains separately registered. `id` is the only profile identity. The old `kind` column is removed; no alias table or replacement string identifier is created.
semantics.recovery_path: recreate registry rows through approved scans, then rescan source files. Preserve the database for user-curated links and review state that may refer to descendant IDs.
semantics.schema_ownership: complete fresh definition in `schema.sql`; `persistence/migrations/` performs a verified backup-backed compatible rebuild to remove `kind` and the retired `enabled` column, supplying `provider_kind` for older schemas. The transaction converts skill FKs, chart scopes, retained workflow boundaries and analysis usage references while retaining Source IDs and child relationships. No explicit named indexes exist. Compatible startup adds absent scan-health columns without rebuilding rows; fresh DDL additionally enforces the bounded status/error checks.

columns.name: id
columns.semantic_contract: `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY`; local scan-evidence identity.

columns.name: source_id
columns.semantic_contract: `INTEGER NOT NULL` FK to `sources.id`, `ON DELETE CASCADE`.

columns.name: session_id
columns.semantic_contract: nullable `INTEGER` FK to `sessions.id`, `ON DELETE SET NULL`; exact normalized Session owner for an accepted Session file, including multi-file native Session sets. Context files remain null.

columns.name: path
columns.semantic_contract: `TEXT NOT NULL`; source-local file identity used for scanner correlation.

columns.name: size_bytes
columns.semantic_contract: `INTEGER NOT NULL`; fingerprint size captured at the latest attempt.

columns.name: mtime_ns
columns.semantic_contract: `INTEGER NOT NULL`; nanosecond file modification fingerprint.

columns.name: last_scanned_at
columns.semantic_contract: `TEXT NOT NULL`; latest attempt time for this input.

columns.name: status
columns.semantic_contract: `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'ok'`; freshness state such as healthy, stale, or error.

columns.name: error
columns.semantic_contract: nullable `TEXT`; bounded scan or parse error evidence.

columns.name: presence_state
columns.semantic_contract: `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'UNKNOWN'`, checked to `PRESENT`, `MISSING`, `UNKNOWN`; independent native Session file presence. Context does not use this observation yet.

columns.name: presence_checked_at
columns.semantic_contract: nullable `TEXT`; UTC time of the latest presence check, including inability to inspect. Null means unverified.

columns.name: presence_error
columns.semantic_contract: nullable `TEXT`; application-bounded (500 characters) reason presence could not be established. It does not replace parsing `error`.

columns.name: session_contract_version
columns.semantic_contract: nullable positive `INTEGER`; provider-specific parser/classification revision used to decide whether the Session, Activity Events, and Session search projection remain current. Null means no known Session revision; Context files remain null.

columns.name: usage_contract_version
columns.semantic_contract: nullable `TEXT`; normalizer contract used to decide whether Usage Records remain current.

columns.name: reference_contract_version
columns.semantic_contract: nullable `TEXT`; generalized Session-reference extractor/reconciler contract used to decide whether the mapped Session evidence remains current.

checks: session_contract_version IS NULL OR (typeof(session_contract_version) = 'integer' AND session_contract_version > 0)
constraints.documented: `UNIQUE(source_id, path)` plus optional physical Session ownership; `session_contract_version` is null or has SQLite storage type `integer` and is greater than zero; `presence_state` is checked to the three independent presence values.

semantics.class_contract: Source-derived observations may retain facts after original files disappear; exact recovery depends on the remaining source and admission state. Owner-deletion rules remain table-specific.
semantics.consumers: `ingest/sync/sessions.py` and `ingest/sync/contexts.py` skip/retry logic, Usage version repair, Session projection repair, multi-file Session-reference aggregation and partial/error sibling repair; `sessions/references.py` uses the mapped current file set for aggregate fingerprints; `sources/queries.py`, `usage/queries.py`, and `local_context/service.py` consume the existing source-status and root lifecycle state. Legacy Atlassian evidence adds an independent extractor/Site fingerprint check before an otherwise-current file is skipped.
semantics.deletion_effect: `source_id` physically cascades from `sources`; optional `session_id` points to `sessions.id` with `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so deleting a Session cannot delete scan evidence before the owning source reconciliation decides its path lifecycle. The legacy correlation from `path` to `sessions.source_path` and the Context correlation to `context_documents.path` remain application-managed. Removing a file row alone does not cascade a Session or Document. Session reconciliation retains absent accepted originals, their owners, search and reference evidence; unavailable or failed source inspection records UNKNOWN after admission. A discovered file may be PRESENT with scan error. Physical replacement paths retire only after the admitted same-native-identity replacement succeeds. Context owns its unchanged successful-root document deletion. Configuration and root-availability failures never authorize normalized-history deletion.
semantics.documented_constraints: `UNIQUE(source_id, path)` plus optional physical Session ownership; `session_contract_version` is null or has SQLite storage type `integer` and is greater than zero; `presence_state` is checked to the three independent presence values.
semantics.lifecycle_contract: Session file rows retain provenance after accepted originals disappear. Presence/check time/reason are separate from parsed fingerprints, error and result versions; old rows initially have UNKNOWN presence. Healthy unchanged inputs remain freshness evidence. A successful scan may remove provider-excluded artifacts and confirmed empty stubs under their own eligibility contracts, without deleting native files. Context file rows keep their separate Local Context lifecycle. An accepted Session path whose parsed content has no Activity Event, Usage Record, or admitted skill observation is also omitted: any prior file row is removed, the native stub remains, and its lack of a freshness row makes later meaningful growth discoverable.
semantics.producers: `ingest/sync/storage.py` inserts and updates scan results for Session and Context services, writes the resolved Session mapping and all three contract versions, and replaces mappings on successful reparse; `ingest/sync/session_files.py` records independent native presence and restores known legacy mappings without inventing parsed versions. Ephemeral analysis accounting parents have no native file registration. `local_context/service.py` removes Context-owned rows when a root is disabled; `persistence/migrations/` compatibly adds the optional Session mapping and three contract fields.
semantics.purpose_and_authority: per-source scan evidence for an accepted local input path, including its file fingerprint, latest attempt state, error, optional normalized Session owner, Session-projection contract version, Usage-normalizer contract version, and generalized Session-reference contract version. Provider-internal files outside the adapter's Session candidate contract never own rows here.
semantics.recovery_path: rescan available owning-source inputs to reconstruct current observations. Exact retained provenance for disappeared Session inputs, including prior parsed fingerprints, result versions and multi-file mappings, requires a database backup. An existing Session can restore a minimal legacy path mapping with scan status `stale`, without claiming parsed fingerprints or result versions; presence is observed independently. Errors and exact prior attempt times are operational history and are not reproduced exactly by a rescan.
semantics.schema_ownership: fresh table definition in `schema.sql`; `persistence/migrations/` compatibly adds `session_id`, `session_contract_version`, `usage_contract_version`, and `reference_contract_version`, separate presence/check/reason fields, and creates `idx_source_files_session` after those columns exist. `persistence/migrations/session_revisions.py` rebuilds this table with a positive-integer-or-null Session revision constraint. Startup validates exact known provider-specific legacy tokens, makes a verified private recovery copy, and converts only their revision numbers while preserving rows, IDs, mappings, fingerprints, other contracts, indexes and foreign keys. Unknown tokens stop startup before schema writes; they are never cast to zero or stamped current. Rebuild accepts only the supported column, outgoing-FK and implicit-uniqueness shapes, with no incoming file FKs. Unknown triggers, check/collation/conflict/ timing/storage modifiers or a pre-existing rebuild target also stop replacement. The rebuild savepoint restores the original table and rows on failure, including an interruption after DROP. This shape refusal is separate from token preflight; it does not promise that unrelated startup migrations made no earlier changes. SQL recognition separates comments, string literals and quoted identifiers; only an actual top-level CHECK matching the known revision predicate proves the numeric contract current. Comments and standalone SQLite BOM whitespace cannot hide unsupported modifiers; keyword text inside quotes cannot create constraints. Literal case is preserved. The exact independent presence-state CHECK is also admitted; other CHECK expressions, even if apparently equivalent, are refused during rebuild rather than assumed safe. For available selected inputs, null Session revisions trigger actual Session/skill reprocessing, even when the independent Usage contract is current; that repair does not reprice Usage. Unavailable inputs retain prior results and versions until actual reprocessing is possible.

columns.name: last_activity_at

columns.name: updated_at

semantics.class: Mixed source identity and curated references
semantics.class_contract: Source-derived identity participates in user-curated links or immutable historical evidence, so delete-and-recreate is not equivalent to an in-place refresh.
semantics.consumers: inventory/detail queries, retrieval, Workstream resource pickers and links, Runner context, activity attribution, and Usage Record attribution/browse joins.
semantics.deletion_effect: physical optional parent of `sessions` and `context_documents`, both `SET NULL`. It is an application target for `project` polymorphic links and `usage_records.workspace_id_snapshot`; those are not cascaded by SQLite.
semantics.lifecycle_contract: mixed source identity and curated references. Session or file-based Document discovery can rebuild path metadata, but Workstream/Thread links and Usage Record snapshot browsing use its stable ID, so delete-and-recreate is not equivalent to update-in-place.
semantics.producers: `ingest/sync/session_store.py` supplies Session working directories and observed activity; `ingest/sync/contexts.py` supplies imported file-based Document parent folders and modification times. Shared `ingest/sync/storage.py` upserts path, display name, Git root, existence, and the latest supplied activity marker; `persistence/migrations/` removes the obsolete `git_branch` column during compatible migration.
semantics.purpose_and_authority: shared canonical path registry discovered from Session working directories and file-based Local Context document folders; the containing Git repository root is current discovery, not historical branch state. Registry membership does not establish that the user opened the path. Sessions Projects separately admits only selected-source paths with eligible primary work Sessions.
semantics.recovery_path: rescan available Sessions or enabled file-based Local Context sources to rediscover their respective paths. Preserve or restore the database to retain stable link targets and historical current-row resolution.
semantics.schema_ownership: fresh definition in `schema.sql`; compatible migration in `persistence/migrations/` drops legacy `git_branch`. No explicit named index.

columns.name: session_class
columns.semantic_contract: `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'work'`; checked to `work` or `maintenance` for rows in `sessions`. `maintenance` identifies retained non-work source Sessions, including linked maintenance Runs and recognized provider-internal helpers. An analysis-only `personal_insight_runs` row has no Session class; its optional usage-accounting parent is `maintenance` with `metadata_only` indexing and is excluded from ordinary Sessions.

columns.name: session_role
columns.semantic_contract: `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'primary'`; checked to `primary` or `subsession`.

columns.name: parent_external_id
columns.semantic_contract: nullable `TEXT`; source-backed parent identity retained even when unresolved.

columns.name: parent_session_id
columns.semantic_contract: nullable self-FK, `ON DELETE SET NULL`; resolved same-source parent.

columns.name: index_policy

columns.name: maintenance_run_id
columns.semantic_contract: nullable unique `TEXT` FK to `maintenance_runs.id`, `ON DELETE SET NULL`; present only for a primary metadata-only Maintenance Session.

columns.name: imported_at

checks: maintenance_run_id IS NULL OR ( session_class = 'maintenance' AND session_role = 'primary' AND index_policy = 'metadata_only' )
constraints.documented: `UNIQUE(source_id, external_id)`, unique nullable `maintenance_run_id`, checks for the two-value class, role, and index-policy vocabularies, and a linked-Session shape check requiring `maintenance`, `primary`, and `metadata_only`. Explicit indexes: `idx_sessions_last_event`, `idx_sessions_workspace`, `idx_sessions_class`, `idx_sessions_role`, `idx_sessions_parent`.

semantics.class_contract: Source-derived observations may retain facts after original files disappear; exact recovery depends on the remaining source and admission state. Owner-deletion rules remain table-specific.
semantics.consumers: Session inventory/detail, dashboard counts, normalized activity, retrieval, Workstream linking/suggestions, Runner context, search projection, Usage Records, and Usage Dashboard denominators. Sessions inventory headline, rows, pagination, and Project grouping share the same `work` plus `primary` denominator with no age cutoff. A selected source matches the stable `sources.id`, not `provider_kind`, so source profiles remain statistically separate even when sharing one adapter.
semantics.deletion_effect: physical `source_id` cascades; optional `workspace_id`, `parent_session_id`, and unique `maintenance_run_id` set null. After a successful scan, missing accepted originals update file presence without deleting their normalized Session or descendants; an available tracked sibling may become its current source path. Failed or unavailable inspection records UNKNOWN, independently from parsing success. In a partially available Session, current evidence adds non-conflicting Events while stored conflicts remain until complete native evidence can establish replacement. Parsed-empty reconciliation is a separate branch: for full-index Sessions, stale conversation/search can be cleared and the Session considered for retirement only when its current owner path belongs to the parsed-empty set AND every tracked sibling path also belongs to that set. A meaningful shared owner, including a source containing only admitted skill observations, prevents that parsed-empty cleanup; retained historical Usage keeps the Session meaningful even after its stale conversation is cleared. Deleting that Session cascades `activity_events`, `usage_records`, derived `session_reference_scans` and `session_reference_evidence`, and the optional user-owned `session_pins` row; scanner also removes its search and source-file projection while preserving a present native stub. A wholly missing source root does not trigger the same stale-file reconciliation. `skill_observations` has no cascading FK and keeps admitted historical uses. Polymorphic links and checkpoint refs are application edges and can retain an unresolved historical ID.
semantics.documented_constraints: `UNIQUE(source_id, external_id)`, unique nullable `maintenance_run_id`, checks for the two-value class, role, and index-policy vocabularies, and a linked-Session shape check requiring `maintenance`, `primary`, and `metadata_only`. Explicit indexes: `idx_sessions_last_event`, `idx_sessions_workspace`, `idx_sessions_class`, `idx_sessions_role`, `idx_sessions_parent`.
semantics.lifecycle_contract: native Sessions are source-derived from meaningful retained native JSONL accepted by the owning provider's Session-candidate contract. Meaningful means the parsed file contains at least one normalized Activity Event, direct Usage Record, or admitted skill observation; metadata-only stubs retain no Session or source-file projection and are reconsidered on later syncs. Conversation normalization retains authored inputs, filters recognized generated context per text block, and reconciles native counterparts using provider-specific precedence. Assistant response phases require explicit provider provenance; absent or ambiguous signals remain unmarked. Claude primary files and direct `subagents/*.jsonl` children are accepted, while deeper internal `subagents` artifacts such as workflow journals are not Sessions. Codex `source.subagent.other=guardian` files remain normalized so their stable source identity, parent relation, and directly observed Usage Records survive, but the parser classifies them as maintenance plus metadata-only: their approval prompts and decisions produce no Activity Events, question counts, search text, or ordinary Session/Subsession presentation. A successful scan reconciles a previously imported row that is no longer an accepted candidate without deleting the native file. Native tools can remove accepted JSONL files under their own retention policies; Claude Code is a confirmed example because it deletes Session files older than `cleanupPeriodDays` at startup. LocalBrain retains already collected Session/Event history when accepted originals disappear; it stores a normalized snapshot rather than a complete raw-transcript archive. Stable IDs, pins, links and Usage survive native cleanup. Available evidence may still update the same identities; unavailable inputs retain their last results and versions. The same native external ID may exist under multiple profiles of one provider because Session identity is unique within `source_id`, not provider kind. A Run-linked primary and its resolved child Sessions keep metadata while maintenance index/event policy is restricted; the private Runner stream is an operational artifact only. Ephemeral personal insight executions are a bounded exception: a retained CLI usage observation creates a metadata-only Maintenance Session accounting parent with identity `localbrain-insight:<Run ID>`. It contains no conversation, events, search entry, workspace, or native source-file registration. The independent Run is its application owner; native-source disappearance does not delete this accounting projection.
semantics.producers: `ingest/sync/session_store.py` plus Claude/Codex parsers create Sessions and Usage Records; parent reconciliation updates self-references and propagates maintenance policy to Claude or Codex children. `maintenance/service.py` synchronizes the selected native source after terminal and recovered Runs. `source_files` versions Session projection freshness independently, allowing classification/parser changes to rebuild Sessions, Activity Events and search. A Session parser-version change rebuilds available projections on the next explicit Sync. Neither operation replaces Usage solely because the Session contract changed. `persistence/migrations/` owns the classification/Run-link constraint repair. `insights/usage.py` separately creates insight accounting parents and canonical Usage Records from observed ephemeral CLI usage.
semantics.purpose_and_authority: one normalized Claude or Codex Session/subsession per stable local source and native external identity. Source key owns provenance and statistical separation, while the Source registry provider kind owns parser and normalization behavior. An in-app Task Runner Run is represented by the selected runner's persisted native primary Session, linked to the Run ledger rather than duplicated by LocalBrain.
semantics.recovery_path: rescan the authoritative native source file and reconcile parents to rebuild imported projections. Native files cannot recreate user-owned `display_title` overrides; retain the database backup for those values. Restoring only a Task Runner stream cannot rebuild a Session or Usage Record; restore the selected runner's native Claude or Codex JSONL and the Run ledger together. The insight accounting exception is recoverable from the independent Run ledger plus retained usage summaries or CLI usage events. A full database rebuild cannot restore retained history whose originals are gone, user-curated links, exact operational history, or confirmed review state without backup.
semantics.schema_ownership: fresh definition and `idx_sessions_last_event`, `idx_sessions_workspace` in `schema.sql`; compatible columns, backup-backed classification/Run-link table repair, and runtime-only `idx_sessions_class`, `idx_sessions_role`, `idx_sessions_parent` in `persistence/migrations/`. Before that structural repair, startup preserves `localbrain.db-pre-maintenance-session-contract-v1.bak` and validates it with SQLite `quick_check`. An older additive layout may have the same approved columns in a different physical order; migration validates every name/type/null/default/key contract, copies values by canonical column name, and converges only the physical order.
